q: When reduced NAD passes its electrons to the first carrier of the electron transport chain, which redox changes occur?
options: NADH is oxidised to NAD+, and the first carrier is reduced
NADH is reduced to NAD+, and the first carrier is oxidised
Both NADH and the first carrier are oxidised at the same time
NADH gains oxygen, while the first carrier loses hydrogen
explanation: Redox reactions are always paired: when one molecule is oxidised (loses electrons), another is reduced (gains them). NADH loses 2 electrons (and an H+) and becomes NAD+; those electrons reduce the first carrier (complex I). Electrons then pass along carriers of increasing electron affinity until they reduce O2.
